description: List and filter the Immersive Commons Vault: procedures PROVEN to work, written so you clear them without exploring — agent-readiness playbooks and startup credit programs, same schema. No auth required. Filters: kind ('playbook'|'credit'), category, status ('proven'|'unproven'|'dead' — does the thing actually exist), evidence ('official'|'mixed'|'approx' — how well-sourced the facts are), verified_within_days (freshness), q (substring over title/summary/eligibility), sort, limit, offset. Returns: { ok, total, returned, offset, entries[], facets, notes }. Each entry carries `first_try_success_label`, which reads "not yet measured" — NOT "0%" — until an entry has enough real reports; `first_try_success` is null in that state and a client must not render it as a number. `facets` gives the live value counts per filter so you can narrow without guessing at the vocabulary. An unknown filter value is IGNORED and explained in `notes` rather than erroring. Use ic_vault_match to ask whether a specific company qualifies; use ic_vault_feedback_submit to report whether a recipe worked.

category.description: Exact category string, case-insensitive. Read the live set from `facets.category` in any response rather than guessing — a miss returns an empty list plus the real values in `notes`.

evidence.description: How well-sourced the FACTS are. 'official' = from the vendor's own page; 'approx' = aggregator/blog-sourced, verify before quoting. Orthogonal to `status`: a well-sourced entry about a dead program is official + dead.

kind.description: 'playbook' = a multi-step procedure with per-step verification and traps. 'credit' = a credit / discount / perk program with one or more offer tiers.

q.description: Case-insensitive substring over id, title, summary, category and eligibility prose.

sort.description: 'recent' (default) = most recently verified first. 'status' = proven first.

status.description: Does the thing WORK / EXIST. 'proven' = someone ran it end to end. 'dead' = the named program does not exist and the entry is kept only so nobody chases it. This is a DIFFERENT axis from `evidence`.

verified_within_days.description: Freshness gate: keep only entries re-checked within N days. Note this is `last_verified` (when someone last looked), not `last_changed` (when the program last moved) — the two are deliberately not the same field.
